Stage E (three references in the order above):
Use case: stylized-concept. Finish an exceptionally well art-directed 16:9 editorial cover for a serious accessible science review, using the attached deterministic geometric studies.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 is the verified spatial layout and identical-unit geometry; image 2 shows the ONE right-handed three-dimensional helical ribbon and its exact reflected left-handed counterpart, enlarged; image 3 is an earlier material/composition study ONLY. Preserve the complete helical ribbon geometry from images 1 and 2, never the inconsistent C-shaped units in image 3.

SCIENTIFIC VISUAL IDEA: a large, quiet reservoir of opposite-handed PAIRS and a small, strongly copper-biased free working population. The viewer first sees a dense, balanced copper-and-graphite whole, then discovers the strongly biased open fringe. An insightful image about the difference between the composition of a whole and the composition of the part that acts. Each core pair retains one copper helix and one exact opposite-handed graphite helix intact. The free fringe has seven copper helices and one graphite helix. All individual helices have the same physical dimensions, pitch, ribbon width and complete single turn, like the prototype pair. Only rigid rotation, perspective and occlusion may change their appearance. Copper and graphite must show opposite spatial winding, not merely different colours. Keep at least one complete boundary pair readable. No growing molecules, no missing or shortened half-turns.

DESIGN: sculptural low relief on a warm bone-white, fine cotton-paper ground; burnished matte copper and charcoal graphite, subtle tactile grain, precise thin edges, coherent soft raking light, deep occlusion at pairs, delicate long shadows. Compose a dense asymmetrical reservoir occupying the left two thirds, with an elegant curved open boundary and a sparse free fringe in the right third. Let the paired units nest closely enough to read as one rich sculptural field. The free units remain clearly separated with airy negative space; same size as core units. Refine the flat technical lighting and basic layout of reference 1 into a distinctive, high-end conceptual artwork, informed by the density, relief and material quality of reference 3. Maintain generous outer margins and a striking silhouette at thumbnail scale. The white surface is a visual separation of populations; keep it as a paper relief, not a literal sorting machine, hole in a laboratory vessel or drainage channel. No external device, arrows or connecting roads.
Use a restrained palette and fine material detail. No text, labels, numbers, formulae, logo, frame, watermark, scientific ball-and-stick structure, medals, human hands or imitation of a named artist. Opaque background.

Stage F (finish-e.png followed by the same module-pair.png):
Edit the supplied editorial cover with ONE precise geometric correction. Preserve its paired-reservoir composition, all the copper forms, dense left field, shadows, paper, palette, material, framing and negative space.
The single isolated CHARCOAL-GREY helix in the open right-hand group (about x=1195,y=525 on the 1672x941 first image) currently winds the same way as the copper helices. Replace ONLY that isolated grey helix with the EXACT OPPOSITE-HANDED grey counterpart shown on the RIGHT in reference image 2. Match the grey units in the paired left field. Reflect the complete copper prototype through a vertical plane: the top sweep must bow toward image-right, the lower sweep toward image-left, as in the right-hand grey reference. Preserve the complete three-dimensional helical turn and length; no change of size, no shortened C or flat curve. Re-render its contact shadow coherently. All other elements stay as they are. No text or marks. Opaque background. This is a conceptual scientific artwork whose meaningful geometry must retain opposite spatial windings.

cover.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original 16:9 editorial cover for an accessible science review of chiral amplification, the nonlinear effects of Kagan and asymmetric autocatalysis of Soai.
Primary request: create a striking sculptural woodcut and embossed-paper still life of handedness becoming predominant through feedback. Two small three-dimensional ribbon helices of the same material wind in opposite handed directions near the start of a single broad curving stream. Along the stream one winding form becomes visibly predominant through repeated sculptural motifs. The stream bends back toward the source in a large open return curve, suggesting a product helping to create more of its own form. The two initial helices must read as opposite windings, not just different colours. Keep this one coherent scene with a clear focal event and generous uncluttered space.
Style and medium: tactile hand-cut woodblock print combined with low embossed-paper relief, crisp expressive cuts, restrained rough ink grain and physical shadows. A quiet but dramatic editorial artwork. Deep midnight-blue ground, ivory relief, copper-rust accents and a little muted sage. Distinguish the two handed forms through their winding geometry and shadow as well as colour.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9. Keep the paired helices, returning stream and the emergence of the predominant form within the central safe area, readable as a 320x180 thumbnail. The repeated modules are abstract geometric sculptures; they do not encode a measured population, a chemical bond structure or an actual reaction vessel.
Constraints: no letters, numbers, equations, labels, axes, logos or watermarks. No human hands, portraits, Nobel medal, robot, brain, circuit board or sci-fi glow. No atom-ball molecular model, no laboratory apparatus, no imitation of a named artist or publication. Opaque background.
